articles.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
articles.description:
Image:
			
This NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope Picture of the Month features galaxies in great detail that have been warped and multiplied like they’ve stepped into a house of mirrors. The brilliant golden galaxies splashed across this image belong to a galaxy cluster called MACS J0454.1-0300. The orange galaxies concentrated on one side of the cluster are not actually part of the cluster and are much farther away from us.
MACS J0454.1-0300 is itself immensely distant: the light from these galaxies has been travelling to us for so long that we’re seeing the cluster as it was when the Universe was about 8 billion years old. While this galaxy cluster is a valuable scientific target in its own right, the real stars of this image are the galaxies that appear warped and stretched, like a painting that has been smeared by a giant hand.
The way these galaxies look is the result of gravitational lensing, in which the enormous mass of a foreground object such as a galaxy cluster bends and magnifies the light from a more distant object in the background. Gravitational lensing allows astronomers to observe galaxies, star clusters and even individual stars that are too far away for our telescopes to see under normal conditions. While the large, orange galaxies appear obviously distorted, look carefully at some of the small reddish background galaxies throughout this picture: even at the very edges of the frame, there are galaxies whose images have been bent into tiny arcs by MACS J0454.1-0300’s gravity.
The gravitationally lensed areas show multiple images of galaxies from when the Universe was young: a group of galaxies 2 billion years after the Big Bang, and a single galaxy just 800 million years old after the Big Bang. The galaxy group appears to be going through a merger, resulting in an enormous burst of star formation.
Astronomers have also identified individual bright ‘knots’ within the gravitationally lensed areas, corresponding to regions as small as 5 light-years across. These tiny clumps appear magnified by a factor of more than 300, in some cases.
A NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope image of this same cluster was released in 2014. Take a moment to compare the two images; the difference between them is dramatic. The new Webb image reveals hundreds of galaxies missing from the earlier image. These galaxies were there all along, but Webb is much more sensitive to their much redder light.
The data behind this image come from two observing programmes (#5058, PI: Furtak; #6882, PI: Fujimoto) that leverage the ability of massive galaxy clusters to bring distant objects into view.
[Image Description: A massive galaxy cluster, made of many golden elliptical galaxies with the largest, brightest one in the centre. Heavily distorted orange galaxies appear all around the cluster, the largest concentrated in a large arc around the cluster's centre; these are images of very distant galaxies, created by gravitational lensing. A few galaxies are large and bluish-white in colour; bright, nearby stars are the same colour.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope's Picture of the Month reveals galaxies in extraordinary detail through gravitational lensing effects. This cosmic magnification showcases the power of modern observatories to peer into the distant universe.

articles.title: New evidence points to two feeding black holes just 175 parsecs apart lurking in the early universe
articles.description: Astronomers have found two actively feeding supermassive black holes separated by just 175 parsecs (570 light-years) in a galaxy seen when the universe was only about 2 billion years old. The system, MG B2016+112, lies at a redshift of 3.273 and is the most compact dual AGN known at this redshift. The study was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Sept. 25.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered two actively feeding supermassive black holes just 175 parsecs apart in the early universe. This remarkable finding provides unprecedented insights into black hole formation and behavior in the cosmos's infancy.

articles.title: James Webb reveals a massive cosmic structure that challenges our understanding of the Universe
articles.description: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope has revealed an ancient galaxy cluster with an unexpectedly dense concentration of dark matter, challenging theories about how the universe developed. The discovery also uncovered a surprising connection between scattered starlight and invisible dark matter that could transform how astronomers study the early cosmos.
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has discovered an ancient galaxy cluster with an unexpectedly dense concentration of dark matter, challenging existing cosmological models. This finding deepens our understanding of the universe's structure and evolution.

articles.title: Scientists make stunning discovery that could help explain why life exists
articles.description: Scientists have discovered that the universe's fundamental physical constants may be finely balanced to make life possible. Even tiny changes to these constants could make liquids too thick or too thin for essential biological processes, potentially preventing life as we know it. Surprisingly, these life-friendly conditions existed billions of years before living cells appeared. The findings raise intriguing questions about why the laws of physics seem so well suited to life.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered evidence that the universe's fundamental physical constants are finely balanced to permit life existence. This remarkable finding suggests the cosmos may be uniquely suited for the emergence of life.

articles.title: Actualité : “L'ère nucléaire de la Nasa” : le vaisseau SR-1, propulsé par fission, part pour Mars dès 2028
articles.description: Le patron de la Nasa, Jared Isaacman, annonce le virage nucléaire de son agence après un accord signé le 8 octobre. Le premier vaisseau interplanétaire propulsé par fission doit décoller pour Mars en 2028, et deux ans plus tard, un réacteur nucléaire devrait …
articles.summary: NASA announces a major shift to nuclear-powered spacecraft, with the SR-1 fission-propelled vessel launching to Mars in 2028. This breakthrough in propulsion technology marks an exciting new era in deep space exploration.

articles.title: ESA's Hera Mission Targets Binary Asteroid Pair in November
articles.description: In just one more month, the European Space Agency’s Hera mission will make history. Moving at 12 kilometers per second versus Earth, the mission is about to rendezvous with the binary Dimorphos-Didymos asteroid pair. NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (D…
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Hera mission will make history this November as it intercepts a binary asteroid pair at 12 kilometers per second. This groundbreaking planetary defense mission will gather crucial data for protecting Earth.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is launching on October 19 aboard Japan's H3 rocket to explore Mars's mysterious moons. This landmark mission will provide unprecedented scientific insights into the Martian system.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: The ESA's Solar Orbiter has discovered and tracked mysterious S-shaped magnetic structures called 'switchbacks' in the solar wind. This breakthrough observation helps scientists understand the dynamic behavior of our Sun.

articles.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.description:
Image:
			Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
articles.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has captured stunning images of stellar jets erupting from a nebula in magnificent detail. This observation reveals the dramatic processes of star formation in unprecedented clarity.

articles.title: Science begins for Smile
articles.description: On 23 September, the European-Chinese Smile mission was declared ready to start revealing how Earth responds to the wind of charged particles from the Sun. This follows a busy in-space commissioning period since the spacecraft launched on 19 May and reached its target orbit for science operations on 20 June.
articles.summary: The European-Chinese Smile mission reached operational status on September 23 and is now beginning its groundbreaking study of Earth's magnetospheric response to solar wind. This collaborative mission opens new windows into planetary magnetism.

articles.title: The Perseverance Rover Reaches Another Milestone
articles.description: NASA's Perseverance Rover has reached another milestone. It now holds the record for the longest distance travelled on another world, meaning Mars and Earth's Moon. It's all thanks the ingenuity behind AutoNav, it's hazard-detection driving system. It's a win for science, as more distance travelled means more scientific objectives are reached.
articles.summary: NASA's Perseverance Rover has achieved a new record by traveling farther on Mars than any rover before it. This milestone demonstrates the remarkable durability and success of our robotic Mars exploration program.

articles.title: Astronomers Uncover More Intriguing Detail in an Ancient Supernova Remnant
articles.description: When a supernova exploded in 1181, Chinese and Japanese sky-watchers recorded it. They couldn't have known what the object was, and why it appeared for six months then disappeared. But in our modern times, we know it was a supernova, and we've even, most likely, found its remnant. New observations reveal more detail than ever in the unusual and rare supernova remnant.
articles.summary: Astronomers have uncovered new details in an ancient supernova remnant originally observed by Chinese and Japanese astronomers in 1181. This interdisciplinary study connects historical records with modern astrophysics.

articles.title: Chandrasekhar Placed A Limit On White Dwarfs, But A New Study Finds This Limit Is Not Absolute
articles.description: The Chandrasekhar limit states that a white dwarf can be no larger than 1.4 solar masses. A new study demonstrates how highly magnetized white dwarfs could overcome that limit, and how such super-Chandrasekhar white dwarfs could form.
articles.summary: A groundbreaking new study demonstrates that the Chandrasekhar limit for white dwarfs is not absolute, challenging a century-old principle. This discovery opens new possibilities for understanding extreme stellar objects.

articles.title: New Data from the Juno Spacecraft Reveals that Jupiter's Has a Rippling, Wavy Magnetodisk
articles.description: Using observations from NASA's Juno spacecraft, an international team led by Shandong University shows that Jupiter's magnetodisk is a rippling structure that rotates with the planet, contrary to what scientists previously thought.
articles.summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft has revealed that Jupiter's magnetodisk has unexpected rippling and wave-like structures. This discovery provides new insights into the dynamic magnetic environment of the gas giant.

articles.title: Green, pink and purple: Astronomers reveal the surprising true colors of white dwarf stars
articles.description: University of Warwick astronomers have shown that white dwarf stars can glow in a range of colors, including the first star ever found that would appear green to the human eye.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: University of Warwick astronomers have discovered that white dwarf stars emit surprising colors beyond white, including green and pink hues. This revelation expands our understanding of stellar composition and appearance in the late stages of stellar evolution.

articles.title: NASA develops batteries to power humanity's return to moon
articles.description: If you've ever had your car start sluggishly, or not at all, on a particularly frigid winter morning, you know standard batteries do not like extreme cold. That's why NASA researchers are working to develop a battery that could function in the brutal cold of the moon's south pole, where nighttime temperatures plunge to minus 328 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 200 degrees Celsius).
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA has developed advanced battery technology designed to power equipment during humanity's return to the Moon. This technological breakthrough is essential for establishing sustained lunar operations and exploration.

articles.title: Trailblazing technique uncovers real shape of scorching-hot exoplanet atmospheres
articles.description: Until now, the alien white-hot worlds of exoplanets have been depicted as circular, but new research has revealed the true shape of their atmospheres to be a deformed sphere rather than a perfect circle.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Astronomers have developed a breakthrough technique revealing the true asymmetrical shape of scorching-hot exoplanet atmospheres, moving beyond previous circular depictions. This advancement enhances our ability to characterize distant worlds and their atmospheric properties.

articles.title: NASA JPL testing readies Voyager technologies lander for moon mission
articles.description: A commercial lander that will be at the forefront of NASA's efforts to establish a moon base, humanity's first lunar outpost, has passed a series of critical tests at the agency's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California. The tests simulated the extreme temperatures and vacuum of space, as well as the intense shaking and ear-splitting roar of launch. Results show that Voyager Technologies' Griffin Mission One (Griffin-1) spacecraft is ready to survive the rigors of space exploration.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA JPL is testing a commercial lander equipped with Voyager-heritage technologies for an upcoming Moon mission. This effort represents progress toward establishing humanity's first sustained lunar base.

articles.title: Scientists may have finally solved the mystery of the Moon’s two faces
articles.description: Scientists may have solved a long-standing mystery about why the Moon’s two sides are so different, using samples collected from its farside for the first time. Their findings suggest that uneven heating from Earth's gravitational pull drove enormous flows of ancient magma, creating the dramatically different lunar landscapes we see today.
articles.summary: Scientists have solved the long-standing mystery of why the Moon's two sides have dramatically different geological characteristics using lunar sample analysis. This breakthrough illuminates the Moon's complex formation and geological history.

articles.title: NASA astronauts splash down after 100 million miles in space
articles.description: NASA’s SpaceX Crew-12 astronauts have returned to Earth after 237 days in space, traveling more than 100 million miles and completing over 3,792 orbits while conducting research to prepare for future missions to the Moon and Mars. The mission also made history with record-setting spacewalk achievements and experiments that could transform medicine both in space and on Earth.
articles.summary: NASA astronauts aboard SpaceX's Crew-12 mission have successfully returned to Earth after 237 days in space and traveling over 100 million miles. This successful mission demonstrates the reliability of commercial crewed spaceflight operations.

articles.title: Planetary genealogy: Milky Way worlds belong to 1 of 2 ‘families,’ scientists find
articles.description: Scientists have performed a cosmic genealogy on planetary systems in the Milky Way, finding two distinct families that influence the evolution and fate of these systems.
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that planetary systems in the Milky Way belong to two distinct families, advancing our understanding of planetary formation and evolution.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship just turned 10 years old. When will it go to Mars?
articles.description: A decade after Elon Musk publicly unveiled plans for the fully reusable megarocket, Starship has reached orbit. How far away is Mars?
articles.summary: SpaceX's Starship reaches orbital capability after a decade of development, marking a major milestone toward realizing Mars exploration missions.

articles.title: FULL LIST: Meet the 2026 Nobel Prize winners
articles.description:
See the full list of the 2026 Nobel Prize winners in Medicine, Physics, Chemistry, and more, celebrating groundbreaking discoveries and contributions.

Read More: https://punchng.com/full-list-meet-the-2026-nobel-prize-winners/
articles.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize winners across Physics, Chemistry, and Medicine are celebrated for groundbreaking discoveries. This recognition honors transformative contributions to science and our understanding of the universe.

articles.title: To Win A Nobel Prize, Go To The Ends Of The Earth
articles.description: Neutrinos are persnickety particles. We couldn't really detect neutrinos from deep space until Francis Halzen had a brilliant, Nobel Prize-winning idea.
articles.summary: Physicist Francis Halzen revolutionized neutrino detection from deep space, overcoming significant technical challenges. His breakthrough work earned recognition for enabling humanity to observe some of the universe's most elusive particles.

articles.title: Actualité : Ce trou béant sur la Lune intrigue les scientifiques depuis 2009 : la Nasa va enfin sonder ce qu’il cache
articles.description: Sur la face visible de la Lune, un puits béant intrigue les planétologues depuis 2009. La NASA vient de retenir une mission robotisée chargée de sonder ses entrailles au radar, au sismographe et au gravimètre, à la recherche d'un tunnel de lave capable d'abri…
articles.summary: NASA will investigate a mysterious pit on the Moon's visible side that has intrigued scientists since 2009. This targeted mission promises to uncover secrets about lunar geology and subsurface features.

articles.title: Mars : la France embarque dans quelques jours dans une aventure spatiale extraordinaire pour explorer un monde encore inconnu
articles.description: Aucune sonde ne s'est encore posée sur Phobos, une des deux lunes de Mars. La mission japonaise MMX, dont le lancement est prévu dans quelques jours, tentera l'exploit et devrait rapporter sur Terre les premiers échantillons de cette lune de Mars. On vous exp…
articles.summary: France joins Japan's groundbreaking MMX mission to explore Phobos, one of Mars' moons, with the spacecraft launching within days. This historic endeavor will be the first spacecraft to land on this unexplored Martian satellite.

articles.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
articles.description: Scientists using the European Space Agency's Mars Express, in combination with a state-of-the-art meteorological model of the Red Planet, have found that there may be some very exotic physics behind Mars’s most curious cloud.
articles.summary: ESA's Mars Express combined with advanced meteorological modeling has revealed that Mars's most distinctive cloud formation is even more unusual than previously thought. This discovery deepens our understanding of Martian atmospheric phenomena.

articles.title: A galaxy spinning out of sync
articles.description:
Image:
			
Though the spiral galaxy in this new image by the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope seems serene, it hides a chaotic secret. This galaxy is NGC 4698, and it lies about 55 million light-years away in the constellation Virgo. It’s one of over one thousand galaxies in the Virgo Cluster, the nearest large cluster of galaxies bound together by gravity.
As a spiral galaxy similar to our own Milky Way galaxy, NGC 4698 has spiral arms that curl around within a thin disc of stars, gas and dust. Its centre is dominated by a galactic bulge.
The diffuse off-white glow of the galaxy’s bulge comes from stars smaller, older, and cooler than the massive blue stars that dot the galaxy’s outer disc. These tightly packed stars orbit a supermassive black hole containing millions of times the Sun’s mass. Scientists have found signs that this black hole is actively growing, drawing gas inward with its gravitational pull.
With a flat, starry disc and diffusely glowing centre, NGC 4698 looks a lot like a typical spiral galaxy — but this galaxy is far from normal. NGC 4698 is one of only a few known spiral galaxies with a bulge that extends out from the disc at a right angle. The elongation is faintly visible in this Hubble image, which shows the ghostly glow of the starry bulge peeking above and below the dusty disc. What’s more, the stars and gas nearest the galaxy’s centre rotate perpendicular to the rest of the disc.
What could cause a galaxy to be so out of sync? Astronomers have found that the culprit likely lies outside the galaxy. If NGC 4698 funneled in gas from an outside source, the newly collected gas could have formed a disc of gas and stars in the galaxy’s centre, at an angle relative to the rest of the disc. Some observations suggest that this galaxy once experienced a minor galactic merger, as evidenced by a short ‘tail’ of hydrogen streaming from one side of the galaxy.
The data used to create this image come from an observing programme (#18103; PI: Thilker) focusing on galaxies in the Virgo Cluster.
[Image Description: A spiral galaxy viewed at an angle, with a bright central bulge and winding spiral arms. The arms form a ring around the galaxy, without appearing to reach its centre. Prominent red-brown dust lanes weave through the arms, which are also dotted with bright blue and reddish regions of star formation. The galaxy is set against a dark background scattered with stars and faint distant galaxies.]
Release on esawebb.org
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has captured a spiral galaxy with intriguing internal dynamics and asymmetries. This detailed observation reveals the hidden complexity within seemingly serene cosmic structures.

articles.title: Astronomers Observe The Limb Darkening Effect On Nearby Stars
articles.description: The edge of the Sun appears darker than its central region. This effect is known as limb darkening and tells us about the solar atmosphere. This same limb darkening effect has now been observed on several nearby stars and could help us improve our understanding of stellar atmospheres.
articles.summary: Astronomers have successfully observed the limb darkening effect on nearby stars, confirming stellar physics predictions. This achievement expands our techniques for studying stellar atmospheres and composition.

articles.title: Curiosity Greets a Spectacular Dawn Sky on Mars
articles.description: Mars is a planetary geologist’s paradise. NASA’s Curiosity rover drove that home recently, with a captivating panorama seen from the slopes of Mount Sharp. The image shows a stunning vista, and was not white-balance adjusted during processing, to show just what a viewer might really see at sunrise standing of Mars.
articles.summary: NASA's Curiosity Rover captured a spectacular panoramic image of a Martian dawn sky, showcasing the beauty of Mars. This imagery exemplifies the ongoing wonder of robotic planetary exploration.
